summary: A GPU worker that fails mid-step stops the engine at once instead of leaving the server hung
compatibility: No user action required. With a container restart policy, the server comes back on its own after such a failure.
details: When one tensor-parallel rank failed inside a step, for example with a CUDA out-of-memory error on TP1, the other ranks waited in the next all-reduce and the engine waited on rank 0. The server stayed up but answered nothing until VLLM_EXECUTE_MODEL_TIMEOUT_SECONDS (300 s) ran out.

Every rank now reports a failure, including ranks that do not return the step's output, and the engine reads replies from all ranks in any order. The first failure stops the engine within a fraction of a second, and the log names the failing rank and its error.
While replies are frequent the wait still spins, as before; when idle it parks on the queue notification, so steps do not get slower.
